thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: SEV2 — elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (svc: inference-runtime). Pager: P12345. Auto-escalation in 5m. Details: 5xx spike from 2026-03-14T17:33:00Z, ~18% error rate, affected region: us-west-2. Links: https://alerts.redwood.internal/p/12345, runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx

alex: I'm the outgoing primary, wrapping up docs. handing over now — root cause unknown yet. I started initial triage: checked pods, noticed restarts on runtime-2.

maria: taking primary. I'll drive mitigation. sgtm? i'm available for the next 4 hours.

alex: +1 maria. i'll stay as secondary for 10m while handoff completes. primary = maria, secondary = alex, comms = ?

sophie: I can own comms and customer updates for the next 2 hours. i'll draft a short note for #customers-prod-updates once we have impact numbers.

tony: I'll be infra fallback (escalation) — ping me if we need node restarts or host-level traces.

maria: plan: 1) confirm whether error is coming from model server or from gateway. 2) if model server, scale a replica and roll that pod. 3) if gateway, route to canary. running quick checks now. runbook pointer: see section "Immediate triage" in the runbook above.

maria: commands I'm running:
```bash
# check recent 5xx traces aggregated by tempo
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/inference-gateway --since=15m | grep \"5xx\" | head -n 50
# list pod restarts
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep runtime
```

alex: logs show a stacktrace pointing at kv-cache eviction in runtime-2. not definitive though. attaching snippet: 
```
2026-03-14T17:31:45Z runtime-2 ERROR kv_cache.cpp: failed to fetch segment id=42
2026-03-14T17:31:46Z runtime-2 WARN backend: falling back to cold load
```

sophie: estimating customer impact: we have ~120 requests/min hitting /v1/generate in us-west-2, error rate ~18% -> roughly 22 failed requests/min. I suggest initial customer blurb: "We're investigating elevated error rates affecting text generation in us-west-2; engineers are actively triaging. We'll update in 30 minutes or as we have new info." Should I post?

maria: yes post the template. add "no data loss" and an ETA of 30m. i'll add a short note once we know cause.

oncall-bot: Reminder: Please set incident severity and assign an incident commander in the incident tracker. Current severity: SEV2.

maria: assigned myself as Incident Commander (IC) in tracker. severity remains SEV2. tagging tony for infra assist if needed.

tony: acknowledged. I'll start checking node metrics and Nvidia driver logs in case of hardware retries. quick check: `dmesg | grep -i nvrm` and GPU util graphs.

alex: small coverage note — there's no overnight oncall overlap between 02:00-06:00 UTC this week due to schedule hole. maria, if this escalates to night, please ping ops-leads to request coverage swap.

maria: noted. current mitigation attempt: scaling runtime deployment +1 replica to absorb evictions. executing `kubectl scale deploy/runtime --replicas=4 -n inference` now.

maria: scaled — new pod coming up. monitoring errors.

sophie: posted initial customer message to #customers-prod-updates and created a short pinned thread: "Investigating elevated errors in us-west-2, IC: maria, comms: sophie." link: https://customers.redwood.com/status/INC-12345

maria: preliminary: error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% after scaling. continuing to watch for 5m window. if stable, we'll plan a canary restart of runtime-2.

alex: thanks team. handoff checklist: 1) IC declared (maria) 2) comms owned (sophie) 3) secondary (alex) for 10m then release 4) infra on standby (tony). all good from me — handing over fully. :white_check_mark:

sophie: i'll continue updates. posting next update in 20m unless heartbeats change. :mag:

maria: will attempt canary restart of runtime-2 in 5 min if error doesn't rebound. marking action items in tracker.

oncall-bot: Scheduled follow-up reminder in 30m for incident status.

tony: if runtime-2 fails healthchecks on restart, escalate to platform-sre for host-level intervention.

maria: last note: runbook section "handoff-specific notes" — make sure to call out comms owner explicitly. this handoff looks clean. handing off fully acknowledged.
